title: Grateful Dead Live at Starlight Theater on 1982-08-03
lineage: [SBD > MC > PCM > DAT > CDR] + [Senn 441's (FOB) > Sony TC-D5 > DAT > CD] > WAV > Vegas 5 (matrix) > WAV > CD Wave > FLAC 16

ai_review.summary: A stunning matrix recording that captures a high‑energy 1982 show with crisp, sweet sound and smoking performances of classics like “Half‑Step → Franklin’s,” “Cumberland Blues,” and “Shakedown Street.”
ai_review.review: The matrix mix is praised as beautiful and crystal‑clear, giving listeners the feeling of being in the crowd while retaining studio‑like balance. The band is described as on fire from start to finish, with Jerry Garcia delivering flawless licks, Brent’s keyboards shining, and standout moments such as the Half‑Step into Franklin’s transition, a ripping “Big Railroad,” and a soaring “Shakedown Street.” Energy is consistently high and the setlist flow receives glowing remarks.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews uniformly rave about both the musical performance and the recording quality; show energy, standout songs, and sound clarity are repeatedly highlighted, yielding a top‑tier rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners note a crisp, sweet, and realistic concert experience with clear vocals, clean guitars and keyboards, and good stereo ambience. Some wish it were an audience recording, but the matrix mix is repeatedly called beautiful and “sweetness” – no major drop‑outs or muddiness reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Transitions are praised (e.g., Half‑Step into Franklin’s, Miss → Frank), set pacing is described as varied but always engaging, and the second set’s mix of rockers and ballads keeps the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly called ‘on’, delivering flawless licks and a storm of guitar work; many reviewers say he was “in total control” and “lit up.”
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s keyboards are highlighted as sounding great in the mix, adding sparkle to the performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are described as good but not exactly like a live sound; occasional jam moments with the drummers receive positive mention.
